prosody.p: Chapter Seven: Managing Money and Measuring What Matters.

As your business starts to grow, managing money becomes a whole lot more important. Now, don’t worry—you don’t need to be an accountant, and you definitely don’t need to get lost in complicated spreadsheets. What really matters is having clarity and paying regular attention to your finances. After all, the real goal here is to make sure your business supports your life—not the other way around.

The first step? Keep your business and personal finances separate. Even just opening a simple checking account for your business income and expenses can make a world of difference. It’ll help you track how profitable you really are, set aside money for taxes, and get a clear picture of where all your money’s going.
Want a few practical habits to keep your business finances healthy? Here are some to try:
Track your income and expenses regularly. Seriously, just use a basic spreadsheet or an easy accounting app—whatever works for you. Log every transaction, even the small ones.
Always set aside money for taxes. A good rule of thumb? Save a percentage from every payment you receive, so there are no surprises when tax season rolls around.
Remember to pay yourself first. Treat your own salary as a must-pay expense, even if you have to start small. You deserve to be compensated for your work!
And finally, review your numbers each month. Look for trends, unexpected costs, or spots where you might be able to save. Sometimes, a quick glance can reveal a lot.

But here’s something to pay attention to—money isn’t the only thing that matters. Sure, financial profit is important, but it’s not the only way to measure success. Think about tracking things like customer happiness, how much freedom you have with your time, or even just your own sense of fulfillment.

For instance, imagine you’re a graphic designer. Maybe you notice that certain clients make your work way more enjoyable, even if those projects don’t pay quite as much. Over time, these little insights can help you decide which jobs you actually want to pursue.

So, here’s the big takeaway—your business exists to support your ideal life, not just to chase the biggest revenue number. By keeping your finances simple and your priorities front and center, you’ll sidestep a lot of the common pitfalls. And you’ll start building a business that feels both secure and truly meaningful.
